fixes.explanation: Verse 2 says it plainly: “And the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.” The earth is formless and void, with darkness over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God is right there over the water. You didn't even need an apron for that one, friend.
The cherubim never show up in this passage. Verse 2 names “…the Spirit of God…” hovering over the surface of the waters. Cherubim sounds so grand that I almost wanted it to be right, friend.

Verse 3 says, “And God said, ‘Let there be light,’ and there was light.” God speaks, and light is what comes. I once spent a whole afternoon looking for a light switch in a kitchen that wasn't mine, so I'm impressed.
Verse 4 says God “…separated the light from the darkness.” Then in verse 5 He calls the light “day,” and the darkness He calls “night.” So each one gets its own name. Two things, two names, friend.
The text says God separated the light from the darkness (verse 4). Nothing in these verses says He blended them. Then in verse 5 each gets its own name, “day” and “night.”

Light is already around by this point, friend, since it came on the first day. But the reason God gives in verse 9 is “…so that the dry land may appear.” Nothing there about light shining on the waters. The waters gather so the dry land may appear.
Seed is the word, friend. Verse 11 says each tree bears “…fruit with seed according to its kind.” Chocolate chips belong in my cookies, but in this verse the seed belongs in the fruit.
Verse 16 says, “God made two great lights: the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night.” So the greater light is the one over the day. Big light, big daytime job, friend.

Yes, friend. Verse 16 says God made “the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night.” So the lesser light is the one over the night. And the verse adds one more thing: “And He made the stars as well.”

That's not what God says in verse 22. He blesses them and says, “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.” That's all about growing and multiplying, with nothing in it about staying put. The words are about filling the waters of the seas and the birds multiplying on the earth.

Rest shows up later in the passage, friend, but it's for God on the seventh day (Genesis 2:2). Here in verse 22, the blessing words are “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters of the seas, and let birds multiply on the earth.” That's about multiplying, not napping.

Verse 26 says man is “…to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air, over the livestock, and over all the earth itself and every creature that crawls upon it.” That's quite a list, friend: fish, birds, livestock, the earth itself and every creature that crawls. Rule is the word God uses.
That's not what verse 26 says, friend. God says man is “…to rule over the fish of the sea and the birds of the air…” The word is rule, and keeping away isn't in the verse at all.

That's not what verse 30 says, friend. God says, “…I have given every green plant for food.” He says it about every beast of the earth, every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth. The verse has God giving the food, so “left on their own” doesn't match its words.

Right, friend. In verse 30 God says, “…I have given every green plant for food.” He says it about every beast of the earth, every bird of the air and every creature that crawls upon the earth, “…everything that has the breath of life in it…” Then the verse ends with “And it was so.”

Verse 31 says, “And God looked upon all that He had made, and indeed, it was very good.” Earlier in the passage, God saw that things were good. Here He looks upon all that He had made, and the word is “very.” Look at that, friend.

Verse 3 says, “…God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it…” So God does two things with this day, friend. He blesses it and He sanctifies it, which means setting it apart as holy. The verse gives the reason: “…because on that day He rested from all the work of creation that He had accomplished.”

Nothing in these verses says the seventh day is longer. What verse 3 says is that “…God blessed the seventh day and sanctified it…” Those are the two things God does with the day. Sorry, friend, no extra hours.
